previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, urostomy, type II diabetes, and polysubstance abuse was admitted after self-inflicting multiple stab wounds to her urostomy site with a screwdriver, reporting she felt 'very very sad.' She underwent an exploratory laparotomy and repair of a small intestinal laceration, along with lysis of adhesions. A Foley catheter was temporarily placed into the urostomy to aid healing. Postoperatively, she developed expected ileus, managed supportively. A loopogram confirmed no leak from the ileal conduit. She gradually advanced to a regular diet, regained bowel function, and was medically stable. Psychiatry and social work addressed her mood disorder, substance use, and housing instability. She was discharged to a wheelchair-accessible shelter with follow-up plans for mental health, primary care, and urology.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman with hx of spinal injury, neurogenic 
bladder with diverting ostomy, Right BKA, left TMA, and diabetes 
who p/w increasing pain in the left foot. 

#Urinary tract infection: After the patient was discharged, her 
urine cx returned positive for >100,000 GNR's. She has 
previously had recurrent infections that have grown Enterococcus 
sensitive to nitrofurantoin. She has done well with this 
antibiotic. The patient was called and asked about symptoms, and 
she reported possible subjective fevers. Therefore, she was 
given a 7-day course of nitrofurantoin. She will be contacted if 
her urine ultimately grows resistant organisms.

# Left Foot/Leg Pain: Exquisite pain to light touch that is 
somewhat distractable from left shin downwards. On the last 
admission, vascular ruled out ischemia as a cause, CTA 
demonstrated a normal triple vessel runoff in the left lower 
extremity. Her pain was felt to be most likely due to peripheral 
neuropathy and improved with gabapentin. The patient reports 
that she hasn't taken any gabapentin since discharge, pain 
improving this admission on gabapentin. She was continued on 
gabapentin and tylenol and narcotics were avoided given history 
of drug-seeking behavior. She was given a prescription for 
gabapentin and a reduced dose of ibuprofen at discharge (had 
been taking above the maximum daily limit); declined tylenol.

#Atypical chest pain: EKG unchanged, was tender to palpation on 
the chest. Pain associated with smoking and cough and 
subsequently resolved. Likely musculoskeletal in nature.

# L heel ulcer: 3cm heel ulcer that appeared after a blister 
popped, now with eschar. Ulcer does not appear necrotic, no 
purulence, surrounding erythema is mild and stable. Got iv vanco 
in the ED until IV infiltrated, then got po doxy/clinda, no 
further antibiotics we given during her hospitalization. She was 
afebrile without systemic symptoms. Wound care saw her and she 
was given education on how to dress her wounds.

#Nasal congestion/L ear pain: Likely viral URI, treated 
symptomatically with guaifenesin and pseudophedrine.   

#Tobacco abuse: was given nicotine patch and lozenges.  smokes 
half a pack a day at baseline. She did leave AMA to smoke while 
inpatient. 

#Chipped tooth: orobase prn

#Social issues: Once the patient was medically stable for 
discharge, placement was difficult as ___ has 
banned her until ___. She was therefore discharged to a shelter 
with a medical respite bed.

CHRONIC ISSUES:  
# Insomnia: Continued trazadone and zolpidem 
 
# Type 2 Diabetes, diet controlled: A1c of 6.3% ___  

# Code: Full (confirmed w/ pt)   
# Emergency Contact: ___ (fiance/HCP) ___  


-Patient has been instructed as to how to dress her wounds once 
she leaves the hospital.
-Follow-up appointments have been scheduled for her at 
Healthcare for the Homeless.
-Her ibuprofen dose was reduced at discharge as she was taking 
above the maximum daily amount of ibuprofen at admission.
-The patient declined to take her vitamin supplements or 
medications for cough at discharge. She said she already has 
medications for her earwax and tooth pain.
-The patient's urine cultures returned positive for GNR's after 
discharge: patient was contacted per above and a 7-day 
nitrofurantoin prescription was called into her pharmacy.
